# Independent audit: actual cap records and ordinary limiting stress

Audited source:
`candidate 714f69e684c396b1`,
Sections 1--7. Result: **PASS**, with no mathematical repair identified.
The supplied checker was rerun with `work/math-venv/bin/python` and passes
112 exact checks. Those checks are supplementary; the measure arguments
below were read independently.

## 1. Finite record map

The coefficient clamp preserves every proper and supporting threshold
exactly, and places the remaining thresholds strictly outside a common
fiber support range. Hence it preserves actual set traces, allocated
surface selectors, and section measures. This is stronger than preserving
cap mass alone. The least-norm feasible coefficient vector belongs to the
span of its active constraint rows: every sufficiently small motion in
their common kernel is feasible in both signs. Choosing an independent
active-row basis gives the stated bounded pseudoinverse formula. Equalities
and deficient base rank cause no problem after quotienting invisible
directions. A Borel choice is available by finitely many active bases.

The source correctly uses the result as an auxiliary record, not as a
replacement of the ambient covering circuit or its integer-normal sum.

## 2. Joint compactness and actual selectors

For each fiber one may choose a fixed center in the limiting interior,
which belongs to all sufficiently late bodies with a common inball. The
radial graph area formula and almost-everywhere convergence of convex
gauges and their gradients give convergence of the boundary measures with
their outer normals recorded. All record and spatial coordinates are
compact. Product measures converge, so domination
`eta_j <= Lambda_j tensor s_j` passes to the limit. The uniform coarea
bound similarly supplies disintegration of the section measure over the
same cap law.

On a region where the limiting cap margin is strictly nonzero, its sign
is eventually constant; this identifies the limiting selector there.
Continuous-normal nondegeneracy makes every cutting hyperplane
d-dimensional-volume-null, including supporting planes. Indicator
convergence away from that plane proves joint captured-volume continuity.
Therefore all records in the support have the actual claimed raw mass.

## 3. Gauss--Green and supporting status

For the captured side `u.X >= tau`, its cut-plane outward normal is
`-u/|u|`. Thus the source's identity

    integral s psi n = integral_cap grad psi + u integral psi d lambda

has the correct sign. At an inside support, deleting the fraction
`1-s` of the facet with normal `-u/|u|` adds
`u(1-s)dS/|u|`; at an outside support the surviving boundary trace gives
`u s dS/|u|`. These are precisely the printed complement/equality rules.
After multiplying by continuous record tests, both volume and boundary
terms pass to the limit. A countable dense family of spatial tests gives
one common almost-everywhere set of records.

Subtracting the ordinary captured-part identity determines the entire
limiting scalar section measure, because `u` is nonzero. In particular no
unaccounted singular mass on section edges remains. The argument also
works for d=1 with endpoint counting measure. The displayed zeroth and
first moment identities are the tests `psi=1` and `psi=X_l`.

## 4. Surviving groups

The source expressly retains a finite contact-label set, own inballs,
the actual same-dual equations, and contact offsets tending to zero.
These assumptions ensure uniformly positive total coarea for every group
cap. Since `kappa_i = integral T_H d Lambda_i`, a group with positive
limiting weight has positive limiting kappa. Its first-moment equality
passes jointly, and the correction is bounded by the largest contact
offset. This proves the common ALLOCATED section mean, which need not be
an integer point or any individual contact.

The contact-gradient bounds and the vanishing offsets imply continuous
normal balance. The record map preserves every contact equation since
its own trace lies in the unchanged threshold range. This proves a cover
at each retained contact of a surviving group; it does not recover
discarded zero-weight groups or a full projected covering circuit.

## 5. Scope and a concrete usable consequence

The physical stress inequality passes on fixed bounded continuous
admissible tests. Its affine-force identities retain outer normals.
No original-volume martingale follows: the volume and coarea weights
are different, and the tilted volume measures may have unbounded mass.
All these restrictions are stated accurately.

One can nevertheless use the resulting cap LAW directly, without a
finite sub-selection, in the paired-roof test of
`candidate fed95f84ea97787a`.
If almost every recorded cap strictly crosses each moving prism between
its paired roofs, then its two boundary selectors add to one. Tonelli
gives the same identity for the total stress density, and the actual
roof-plane convex penalties yield a positive response at beta<1/2.
This is conditional on actual crossing geometry; the compactification
theorem does not automatically provide that geometry.

The source's interval limits correctly show why inside allocations need
not remain zero, and why a trace-preserving clamp may still change the
integer-normal resultant. There is no hidden finite-menu or OC conclusion.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
